Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 60, verse 1:

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, showing them affection, when they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth, expelling the Messenger and you [merely] because you believe in Allah, your Lord. If you have come out striving in My way and seeking My approval, [would you] confide to them with affection? I am most knowing of what you conceal and what you declare. And whoever of you does that has certainly strayed from the sound way.﴾ (1)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, is saying to the believers among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy﴾ from among the polytheists ﴿and your enemy as allies﴾, meaning as helpers (ansar).

* *

As for His words: ﴿you show them affection﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, is saying: you convey to them your affection for them. The presence or absence of the preposition bi- in His words ﴿bil-mawaddah (with affection)﴾ is equivalent, like the speaker's saying: "I want to that you go" and "I want that you go" are the same, and like His words: ﴿and whoever intends therein deviation by wrongdoing﴾, meaning: whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing. Among this is the saying of the poet:

"When they were about to drink, he struck them with the staff,
a miser who, at the watering trough, is wrathful."

Meaning: when they were about to drink (rajat al-shurb). [[The line is among the evidences cited by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 330) at His words "you show them affection." He said: the presence of the preposition bi- before mawaddah and its absence are the same; this is like "I think that you are standing" and "I think you are standing," and "I want you to go" and "I want to go." Allah has said: "and whoever intends therein deviation by wrongdoing," where He used bi-. The meaning is: whoever intends therein deviation. Abu al-Jarrah recited to me: "When they were about to drink... the line," meaning: when they were about to drink. End of quotation. Al-Izza' is the trough from which camels drink. Al-Nuhaym is a sound of rebuke and threat. The author had already cited this line in Surah al-Hajj at His words "and whoever intends therein deviation" (vol. 17, p. 139). In the text of the line there, "al-Ada'" appears in place of "al-Izza'" here; this is a printing error, and the word should be corrected to "al-Izza'" as here, which is the trough.]]

﴿And they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth﴾ means: these polytheists whom I forbade you to take as allies have disbelieved in what came to you from Allah of the truth. That disbelief is their disbelief in Allah, His Messenger, and His Book which He sent down to His Messenger.

* *

As for His words: ﴿expelling the Messenger and you﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, is saying: they expel the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and you, meaning: they also expel you from your homes and your land. That was the expulsion by the polytheists of Quraysh of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions from Makkah.

* *

As for His words: ﴿that you believe in Allah, your Lord﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, is saying: they expel the Messenger and you from your homes because you believed in Allah.

* *

As for His words: ﴿If you have come out striving in My way and seeking My approval﴾

This is from the postponed (al-mu'akhkhar) word order whose meaning is the anterior. The construction of the speech is: "O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, showing them affection, when they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth, if you have come out striving in My way and seeking My approval. [They are] expelling the Messenger and you because you believe in Allah, your Lord."

And the meaning of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿If you have come out striving in My way﴾ is: if you have come out from your homes, emigrating from them to your places of emigration for striving (jihad) on My path, which I have prescribed for you, and My religion, which I have commanded you to follow, and seeking My approval.

* *

As for His words: ﴿you confide to them with affection﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, is saying to the believers among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): you, O believers, confide with affection to the polytheists who associate others with Allah. ﴿And I am most knowing of what you conceal﴾ means: I know better than you what some of you conceal from others and keep secret from them. ﴿And what you declare﴾ means: and I also know better than you what some of you declare to others. ﴿And whoever of you does that has certainly strayed from the sound way﴾: He, may His praise be exalted, is saying: whoever of you, O believers, confides to the polytheists with affection has strayed, meaning he has deviated from the right way which Allah made a path to Paradise and a road leading to it.

It is mentioned that these verses at the beginning of this surah were revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah. He had written to Quraysh in Makkah informing them of a matter which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had concealed from them. Reports and narrations to this effect have come from a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and others.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ubayd ibn Isma'il al-Habbari and al-Fadl ibn al-Sabah narrated to me, both saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi' informed me, saying: I heard 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me, al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, and al-Miqdad, — al-Fadl said, Sufyan said: a group of the Muhajirun — and said: "Set out until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman traveler (zu'ayna) with her a letter; take it from her." So we set out, our horses galloping with us, until we reached the garden, and we found a woman. We said: "Bring out the letter." She said: "I have no letter with me." We said: "You will surely bring out the letter, or we will strip off your garments." So she took it out from her braids (mi'saf), and we took the letter and brought it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). In it was: "From Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah to some people in Makkah, informing them of some of the affair of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Hatib, what is this?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, do not hasten against me. I was a man attached to Quraysh, but I had no kinship with them, and those of the Muhajirun who are with you have kinsfolk who protect their families in Makkah. So I wished, since I had missed that lineage tie, to make for myself a hand among them by which they would protect my relatives. I did not do this as disbelief or apostasy from my religion, nor out of contentment with disbelief after Islam." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He has told you the truth." Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, let me strike the neck of this hypocrite." He said: "He has indeed witnessed Badr. What would make you know? Perhaps Allah has looked upon the people of Badr and said: 'Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you.'" Al-Fadl added in his narration, Sufyan said: and concerning him this was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾ ... to His words: ﴿until you believe in Allah alone﴾.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Sinan Sa'id ibn Sinan, from 'Amr ibn Murrah al-Jamali, from Abu al-Bakhtari al-Ta'i, from al-Harith, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to go to Makkah, he confided to some of his Companions that he intended Makkah, among them Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah. He spread among the people that he intended Khaybar. Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah wrote to the people of Makkah that the Prophet (ﷺ) was coming against them. He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) sent me and Abu Murthad, and there was not a man among us but who had a horse. He said: "Go to Rawdat Khakh, for you will meet a woman there, and with her is a letter; take it from her." So we set out until we saw her at the place the Prophet (ﷺ) had mentioned. We said: "Bring the letter." She said: "I have no letter." We placed her belongings down and searched, but we did not find it among her belongings. Abu Murthad said: "Perhaps it is not with her." I said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) has not lied, nor has he been lied to." We said: "Bring out the letter, or we will strip you bare." Amr ibn Murrah said: she brought it out from her waistwrap (hujzah). Habib said: she brought it out from her front, and we brought it to the Prophet (ﷺ), and behold, the letter was: "From Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah to the people of Makkah." Umar stood up and said: "He has betrayed Allah and His Messenger. Permit me to strike his neck." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Has he not witnessed Badr?" He said: "Yes, but he has broken faith and has backed your enemies against you." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Perhaps Allah has looked upon the people of Badr and said: 'Do whatever you wish.'" Umar's eyes overflowed and he said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He sent for Hatib and said: "What prompted you to do what you did?" He said: "O Prophet of Allah, I was a man attached to Quraysh, and I had there family and wealth, and none of your Companions has but has in Makkah someone who protects his family and property. So I wrote to them about this. By Allah, O Prophet of Allah, I truly believe in Allah and His Messenger." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah has spoken the truth, so say nothing to Hatib but good." Habib ibn Thabit said: then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy﴾ ... the verse.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, my paternal uncle narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, showing them affection﴾ ... to the end of the verse: it was revealed concerning a man of Quraysh who was with the Prophet (ﷺ) in Madinah, who wrote to his family and clan in Makkah, informing them and warning them that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was marching toward them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was informed of his letter, so he sent 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who brought it to him.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and others from our scholars, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) resolved to march to Makkah, Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah wrote a letter to Quraysh informing them of what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had resolved upon regarding marching against them. Then he gave it to a woman, whom Muhammad ibn Ja'far claimed was from Muzaynah, while others claimed she was Sarah, a freedwoman of some of the Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib, and he gave her a reward on condition that she deliver it to Quraysh. She placed it in her hair, then braided over it her locks, and set out. Then news came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from heaven about what Hatib had done, so he sent 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, may Allah be pleased with them both, and said: "Overtake a woman with whom Hatib has sent a letter to Quraysh warning them of what we have resolved upon regarding them." They set out until they overtook her at Hulayfat Ibn Abi Ahmad, and made her come down, and searched her saddlebag, but they found nothing. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said to her: "I swear by Allah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has not lied, nor have we been lied to. You will surely bring out this letter to me, or we will strip you." When she saw his determination, she said: "Turn away from me," and he turned away from her. She untied her braids, brought out the letter, and handed it to him. He brought it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who summoned Hatib and said: "O Hatib, what prompted you to this?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I truly believe in Allah and His Messenger. I have not changed nor altered. But I was a man among the people with no lineage or clan, and I had among them family and children, so I made an arrangement with them concerning them." Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Let me, O Messenger of Allah, strike his neck, for the man has become a hypocrite." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What would make you know, O Umar? Perhaps Allah has looked upon the companions of Badr on the day of Badr and said: 'Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you.'" Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning Hatib: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾ ... to His words: ﴿And to You we have turned in repentance﴾ ... to the end of the story.

* 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, who said: When it was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾ concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, he wrote to the disbelievers of Quraysh a letter advising them. Allah informed His Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace, of that, so he sent 'Ali and al-Zubayr and said: "Go, for you will surely find a woman at such and such a place; bring the letter that is with her." They set out until they overtook her, and they said: "The letter that you have." She said: "I have no letter." They said: "By Allah, we will not leave anything with you without searching it, or you will bring it out." She said: "Are you not Muslims?" They said: "Yes, but the Prophet (ﷺ) has informed us that you have a letter, and our souls are certain that it is with you." When she saw their determination, she brought out a letter from between her braids. They took it to the Prophet (ﷺ), and behold, it said: "From Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah to the disbelievers of Quraysh." The Prophet (ﷺ) summoned him and said: "Did you write this letter?" He said: "Yes." He said: "What prompted you to that?" He said: "By Allah, I have had no doubt about Allah since I embraced Islam, but I was a stranger among you, O clan of Quraysh, and I had wealth and sons in Makkah, so I wished to ward off harm from them by this." Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Permit me, O Messenger of Allah, to strike his neck." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Gently, O son of al-Khattab. What would make you know? Perhaps Allah has looked upon the people of Badr and said: 'Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you.'" Al-Zuhri said: concerning this was revealed up to ﴿Forgiving, Merciful﴾.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿Do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾ ... to His words: ﴿Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do﴾, concerning the correspondence of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah and his companions with the disbelievers of Quraysh, warning them.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾ ... until He reached ﴿the sound way﴾: It has been mentioned to us that Hatib wrote to the people of Makkah informing them of the march of the Prophet (ﷺ) toward them at the time of al-Hudaybiyah, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed His Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace, of that. It was also mentioned to us that they found the letter with a woman in a braid of her hair. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) summoned him and said: "What prompted you to what you did?" He said: "By Allah, I did not doubt the command of Allah, nor did I apostatize regarding it, but I have family and wealth there, and I wanted to make an arrangement with Quraysh to protect my family and my wealth." It was also mentioned to us that he was an ally of Quraysh, not one of their own, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the Qur'an concerning that, saying: ﴿If they overcome you, they will be your enemies and will extend toward you their hands and tongues with evil, and they wish that you would disbelieve﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 60, verses 2–3:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿If they overcome you, they will be your enemies and will stretch out their hands and their tongues against you with evil, and they wish that you would disbelieve (2). Your relatives and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection; He will separate between you, and Allah is Seeing of what you do (3).﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "If these people, whom you, believers, show affection to, overcome you, they will be enemies and hostile to you," ﴿and will stretch out their hands﴾ with fighting, ﴿and their tongues with evil﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and they wish that you would disbelieve﴾

He says: and they wish for you to disbelieve in your Lord, so that you would be upon the same [state] as they are upon.

* *

His saying: ﴿Your relatives and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Let not your relatives, kinsfolk and children call you to disbelief in Allah and to taking His enemies as allies, to whom you extend affection, for your relatives and your children will not benefit you with Allah on the Day of Resurrection, so as to ward off Allah's punishment from you on that day, if you disobey Him in the world and disbelieve in Him.

* *

His saying: ﴿He will separate between you﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: Your Lord, O believers, will separate between you on the Day of Resurrection by admitting the people of His obedience to Paradise and the people of disobedience and disbelief in Him to the Fire.

The reciters differed in the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Madinah, Makkah and Basra read ﴿yufṣalu baynakum﴾ with a dammah on the yā' and a light ṣād, with a fatḥah on it, in the passive form (the subject not named) (i.e., the passive voice, with the agent unstated).

The majority of the reciters of Kufa, except ʿĀṣim, read it with a dammah on the yā' and a doubled ṣād, with a kasrah, meaning: "Allah will separate between you, O people." ʿĀṣim read it with a fatḥah on the yā' and a light ṣād with a kasrah, meaning: "Allah will separate between you." Some reciters of Syria read ﴿yufaṣṣilu﴾ with a dammah on the yā', a fatḥah on the fā', and a doubled ṣād, in the passive form.

These readings are close in meaning and sound in their grammatical construction (iʿrāb), so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.

* *

His saying: ﴿and Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: And Allah, O people, has knowledge and sight of your deeds; nothing of them is hidden from Him, He encompasses all of them, and He will recompense you for them, good for good and evil for evil. So fear Allah regarding yourselves and beware of Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 60, verse 4:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, "Indeed, we are free of you and of what you worship besides Allah. We have rejected you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone," except for the saying of Abraham to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you, though I have not power for you against Allah at all. Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have turned in repentance, and to You is the destination."﴾ (4)

His exalted remembrance says to the believers among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "There has already been for you, O believers, an excellent example (uswah hasanah)": that is, an excellent model in Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful (Khalil al-Rahman), whom you follow, and those with him from among the prophets of Allah.

As:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him﴾. He said: "Those with him are the prophets."

* *

And His saying: ﴿when they said to their people, "Indeed, we are free of you and of what you worship besides Allah"﴾

He says: when they said to their people who disbelieved in Allah and worshipped the false deities: "O people, indeed we are free of you, and of those you worship besides Allah, of the gods and rivals."

* *

And His saying: ﴿We have rejected you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone﴾

His majestic praise says, reporting the speech of His prophets to their disbelieving people: "We have rejected you": we denied what you were upon of disbelief in Allah, and we repudiated your worship of what you worship besides Allah as being true; and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever, because of your disbelief in Allah and your worship of other than Him, and there is no reconciliation between us and no leniency, "until you believe in Allah alone": that is, until you affirm Allah alone, so that you make Him one and single Him out in worship.

And His saying: (except for the saying of Abraham to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you, and I have no power for you against Allah at all") His exalted remembrance says: "There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him in these matters we have mentioned, of separating from the disbelievers and opposing them, and abandoning allegiance to them, except in the saying of Abraham to his father, ﴿I will surely ask forgiveness for you﴾, for there is no example for you in that, because that was from Abraham to his father due to a promise he had made to him before it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah; so when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disowned him." His exalted remembrance says: "Likewise you, O believers in Allah, disown the enemies of Allah from among the polytheists and do not take them as allies until they believe in Allah alone and disavow the worship of anything else, and show them enmity and hatred."

The people of interpretation said what we have said in this regard.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿except the saying of Abraham to his father﴾, he said: "They were forbidden to take as an example Abraham's asking forgiveness for his father, so that they would not ask forgiveness for the polytheists."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ja'far, from Mutarrif al-Harithi, from Mujahid: ﴿an excellent example in Abraham﴾ ... up to His saying: ﴿I will surely ask forgiveness for you﴾, he said: "In all his affairs he is an example, except the seeking of forgiveness for his father."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham﴾ ... the verse: "Take him as an example in everything, except his saying to his father, ﴿I will surely ask forgiveness for you﴾; do not take that as an example from him, for it was from a promise he had made to him."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿except the saying of Abraham to his father﴾, he said: "Do not take that as an example, for it was a promise he had made, but take his whole affair as an example."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example﴾ ... up to His saying: ﴿except the saying of Abraham to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you"﴾, he said: "He says: you have no example in this."

By His saying: ﴿I have no power for you against Allah at all﴾ He means: I cannot repel from you any punishment from Allah, since Allah punishes you for your disbelief in Him, nor can I avail you anything against Him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Our Lord, upon You we have relied﴾

His majestic praise, reporting the speech of Abraham and his prophets, peace be upon them, says: ﴿Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have turned in repentance﴾, meaning: and to You we have returned in repentance from what You dislike to what You love and are pleased with; ﴿and to You is the destination﴾, He says: and to You is our destination and our return on the day You resurrect us from our graves and gather us on the Day of Resurrection to the place of reckoning.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 60, verses 5–6:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord. Indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise (5). There has certainly been for you in them an excellent pattern for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever turns away – indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy (6).﴾

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿It may be that Allah will bring about affection between you and those of them with whom you have made enemies. And Allah is Competent﴾ over that ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: He forgives many sins and is merciful to His servants.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes - from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them.﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion﴾ from the people of Makkah, ﴿and do not expel you from your homes - from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them﴾. That is, "and deal equitably with them by your kindness to them and your goodness toward them."

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning those whom this verse refers to. Some of them said: It refers to those who had believed in Makkah but did not emigrate, so Allah permitted the believers to show goodness and kindness to them.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion﴾, [that means] that you seek forgiveness for them, ﴿from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them﴾. He said: They are those who believed in Makkah and did not emigrate.

Others said: It refers to those who were not from the people of Makkah and did not emigrate.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Anmati narrated to me, saying: Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Sari narrated to us, saying: Mus'ab ibn Thabit narrated to us, from his paternal uncle 'Amir ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, who said: It was revealed concerning Asma' bint Abi Bakr. She had a mother in the Jahiliyyah called Qutayla bint 'Abd al-'Uzza, who came to her with gifts, clarified butter, dried curd and ghee. She [Asma'] said: I will not accept a gift from you, and do not enter upon me until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gives permission. She mentioned that to 'A'isha, and she told the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so Allah revealed: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion﴾ ... up to His saying: ﴿the just﴾.

[Another chain:] Ibrahim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: Mus'ab ibn Thabit narrated to us, from 'Amir ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, who said: Qutayla bint 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn Sa'd of Banu Malik ibn Hisl came to her daughter Asma' bint Abi Bakr, and he mentioned something similar.

Others said: Rather, it refers to those among the polytheists of Makkah who did not fight the believers and did not expel them from their homes. He said: Allah later abrogated that by the command to fight them.

Those who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Allah does not forbid you﴾ ... the verse, and he said: This has been abrogated; fighting abrogated it. They were commanded to proceed against them with swords, to fight them with them, striking them, and Allah set for them a term of four months, after which it was either slaughter or Islam.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah does not forbid you﴾ ... the verse, he said: It was abrogated by ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾.

The most correct of these opinions is the view of those who said: What is meant is: Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion, from all categories of creeds and religions, from being righteous toward them, maintaining ties with them, and acting justly toward them. Allah, mighty and majestic, generalized by His saying: ﴿those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes﴾ all who have this description, and He did not specify some of them over others. There is no sense in the view of those who say that it is abrogated, because the righteousness of a believer toward people of war with whom there is a blood relation, or with whom there is no relation or blood tie, is not forbidden or prohibited, provided that there is no indication in it of a weakness of the Muslims exposed to the enemy, or support for them with horses or weapons. The report we mentioned from Ibn al-Zubayr regarding the story of Asma' and her mother has clarified the soundness of what we have said on this matter.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly﴾

He says: Indeed Allah loves those who are equitable, who give people their rights and justice from themselves, so they show kindness to those who show kindness to them and do good to those who do good to them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 60, verse 9:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿God only forbids you from those who fight you over religion, and expel you from your homes, and back up [others] in your expulsion, that you make allies of them. And whoever makes allies of them, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.﴾ (9)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿God only forbids you﴾ O believers ﴿from those who fight you over religion﴾ of the disbelievers of the people of Mecca ﴿and expel you from your homes, and back up [others] in your expulsion﴾ meaning: and aid those who expelled you from your homes in expelling you, ﴿that you make allies of them﴾, so that you become their allies and helpers. ﴿And whoever makes allies of them﴾ meaning: and whoever takes them, from among you or from others, as allies ﴿then it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾ meaning: then they are those who have taken as allies what it is not permissible for them to take as allies, have placed their alliance in other than its proper place, and have opposed God's command in that.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of His saying: ﴿those who fight you over religion﴾.
