The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, then test them. God is most knowing of their faith. And if you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers. They are not lawful [wives] for them, nor are they lawful for them [as husbands]﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to the believers among the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ: ﴿O you who have believed, when come to you﴾ the women ﴿believing women as emigrants﴾ from the house of disbelief to the house of Islam ﴿then test them﴾. And the Messenger of God's ﷺ testing of them was when they arrived as emigrants.

As:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Qays ibn al-Rabi', from al-Aghharr ibn al-Sabah, from Khalifa ibn Husayn, from Abu Nasr al-Asadi, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked: How was the testing of the women by the Messenger of God ﷺ? He said: He would test them by God: "Did you not leave out of hatred for a husband? By God, did you not leave out of aversion to one land for another? By God, did you not leave out seeking worldly gain? By God, did you not leave out only out of love for God and His Messenger?"

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Atiyya narrated to us, from Qays, who said: al-Aghharr ibn al-Sabah informed us, from Khalifa ibn Husayn, from Abu Nasr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, then test them﴾: he said, "When a woman came to the Messenger of God ﷺ, he would make her swear by God that she had not left..." Then he mentioned something similar.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, that A'isha said: The Messenger of God ﷺ tested believing women only by the verse, God said: ﴿When believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with God﴾ and so on.

⁕ Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Urwa ibn al-Zubayr informed me that A'isha, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: When believing women emigrated to the Messenger of God ﷺ, they were tested by God's saying: ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you﴾ ... to the end of the verse. A'isha said: Whoever among the believing women acknowledged this had acknowledged the love [of God and His Messenger]. When they affirmed this in their words, the Messenger of God ﷺ would say to them: "Go, for I have given you allegiance." By God, the hand of the Messenger of God ﷺ never touched the hand of a woman, except that he pledged allegiance to them with words. A'isha said: By God, the Messenger of God ﷺ never took pledges from women except as God, mighty and majestic, commanded him, and when he took their pledge he would say to them, "I have given you allegiance," in words.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding his saying: ﴿O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants﴾ ... to His saying: ﴿Knowing, Wise﴾: their testing was that they bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿then test them﴾: he said, "Ask them what brought them. If what brought them was anger at their husbands, or resentment, or something else, and they have not believed, then return them to their husbands."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿then test them﴾: their testing was that they be made to swear by God that nothing brought them out except rebellion (nushuz), and that nothing brought them out except love of Islam and its people and eagerness for it. When they said that, it was accepted from them.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿then test them﴾: he said, "They swear that they did not leave except out of desire for Islam and love of God and His Messenger."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father or Ikrima, regarding ﴿when believing women come to you as emigrants, then test them﴾: he said, "It is said: Nothing brought you except love of God; nothing brought you the infatuation with a man from among us, nor flight from your husband." That is His saying: ﴿then test them﴾.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "A woman among the polytheists, when she was angry at her husband and there was a dispute between them, would say: 'By God, I will emigrate to Muhammad ﷺ and his companions.' Then God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿When believing women come to you as emigrants, then test them﴾. If anger brought her, return her; if Islam brought her, do not return her."

⁕ Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to me, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, who said: Their testing was: "Only religion brought you out."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿God is most knowing of their faith﴾

He says: God is most knowing of the faith of the women who came to you as emigrants.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers﴾

He says: If they affirm, at the time of the testing, that which validates for them the contract of faith and entry into Islam, then do not return them at that point to the disbelievers. This was said to the believers only because the agreement that had been made between the Messenger of God ﷺ and the polytheists of Quraysh at the Treaty of Hudaybiyya was that the Muslims would return to the polytheists whoever came to them as a Muslim. God annulled that condition with regard to women who came as believing emigrants and were tested; the Muslims found them to be believers, and this was established for them by what we mentioned earlier. They were commanded not to return them to the polytheists once it was known that they were believers. And He, whose praise is great, said to them: ﴿And if you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers. They are not lawful [wives] for them, nor are they lawful for them [as husbands]﴾, meaning: the believing women are not lawful for the disbelievers, nor are the disbelievers lawful for the believing women.

Reports have come in accordance with what we have said on this matter.

Mention of some of the report transmitted on this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, who said: "I entered upon Urwa ibn al-Zubayr while he was writing a letter to Ibn Abi Hunayd, the agent of al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik, and he wrote to him asking about the saying of God, mighty and majestic: (When believing women come to you as emigrants) ... to His saying: ﴿God is Knowing, Wise﴾. Urwa ibn al-Zubayr wrote to him: The Messenger of God ﷺ had made a treaty with the Quraysh in the year of Hudaybiyya that he would return to them whoever came to him without the permission of his guardian. When women emigrated to the Messenger of God ﷺ and to Islam, God refused that they be returned to the polytheists once they had been tested with the test of Islam, and it became known that they had come desiring it."

The commentary on the words of God, the Exalted: ﴿And give them what they have spent, and there is no blame upon you to marry them when you have given them their bridal payments. And do not hold on to marriage bonds with disbelieving women, and ask for what you have spent and let them ask for what they have spent. That is the judgement of Allah; He judges between you. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾ (10)

As for His words, ﴿And give them what they have spent﴾:

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: Give the polytheists whose women have come to you as believers, once you know that they are believers, and you do not return them to them, what they spent in marrying them, namely the bridal payment (ṣadāq).

Those who interpret the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants...﴾ to His words: ﴿Knowing and Wise﴾, he said: Their testing was that they would testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger. When they knew that this was true from them, they did not return them to the disbelievers, and he gave their husbands from among the disbelievers, with whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had made a treaty, the bridal payment that he had given her.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And give them what they have spent﴾: and give their husbands their bridal payments.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, test them; Allah is most knowing of their faith﴾ up to ﴿Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾. This is a ruling that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, issued between the people of guidance and the people of misguidance. When they fled from the polytheists who had a treaty between them and the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions to the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) and they married them, they sent their bridal payments to their husbands among the polytheists with whom there was a treaty between them and the Prophet (ﷺ). And when they fled from the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) to the polytheists with whom there was a treaty between them and the Prophet (ﷺ), they sent their bridal payments to their husbands among the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: It was revealed to him while he was at the bottom of al-Hudaybiyah, and the Prophet (ﷺ) had made peace with them that whoever came to him from them he would return to them. When the women came to him, this verse was revealed to him, and he was commanded to return the bridal payment to their husbands. A ruling was made against the polytheists similar to that: if a Muslim woman came to them, they were to return the bridal payment to her husband. So He said: ﴿And do not hold on to marriage bonds with disbelieving women﴾.

I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿Allah is most knowing of their faith﴾: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) had made a covenant with polytheists and with People of the Book; he made a covenant with them and they with him, and the condition was that they would return property and women. When one of the wives of believers escaped and joined the covenanted people, abandoning her religion and choosing polytheism, the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) returned to her husband what he had spent on her. And when one of the wives of polytheists joined the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) tested her, asking her what had driven her out from her people. If he found that she had left wanting Islam, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted her and returned to her husband what he had spent on her. But if he found that she had fled from her husband to another with whom she had kinship, and she was clinging to polytheism, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned her to her polytheist husband.

Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, test them...﴾ the whole verse: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a truce with the polytheists, "among the condition he stipulated was that you return to us whoever comes to you from us, and we will return to you whoever comes to us from you." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever comes to us from you, we will return him to you; and whoever comes to you from us and chooses disbelief over faith, we have no need of them." He said: Allah refused this for the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding the women, but did not refuse it regarding the men. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿When believing women come to you as emigrants, test them...﴾ to His words: ﴿And give them what they have spent﴾ to their husbands.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, who said: There was a truce between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the polytheists concerning those women who fled. When a polytheist woman fled, the Muslims gave her husband the expenses he had spent on her, and the Muslims used to do this. And if neither side gave back, the Muslims would take from the Muslim man whose wife had gone the expenses she had cost.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And there is no blame upon you to marry them when you have given them their bridal payments﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: There is no sin upon you, O believers, to marry these emigrant women who have joined you from the abode of war, separated from their husbands, even if they have husbands in the abode of war, once you know them to be believers, when you give them their bridal payments. By "their bridal payments" he means the ṣadaqat. Qatadah used to say: When they fled from the polytheists who had a treaty between them and the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions to the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) and married them, they sent their bridal payments to their husbands among the polytheists with whom there was a treaty between them and the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Bishr related this to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah. And al-Zuhri used to say: Allah only commanded the return of their bridal payments to them when they were withheld from them, and if they returned to the Muslims the bridal payments of those women whom they had withheld from them.

Ibn Humayd related this to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri: Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And there is no blame upon you to marry them﴾, "and she has a husband (still)," because Islam separates them once they have completed the waiting period for their wombs.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And do not hold on to marriage bonds with disbelieving women﴾:

He, may His praise be exalted, says to the believers among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): Do not hold on, O believers, to the bonds and ties of disbelieving women. "Kawafir" is the plural of "kafirah," and "'isam" is the plural of "'ismah," which is what is held onto of a contract or tie. This is a prohibition from Allah to the believers against proceeding to marry polytheist women from the people of idols, and a command to them to separate from them.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak related to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan ibn al-Hakam: that women who were believers came to the Prophet (ﷺ) after the document of the agreement had been written between him and Quraysh. So Allah revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants...﴾ until ﴿with disbelieving women﴾. 'Umar then divorced two wives he had who were polytheists: one of them was married by Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan and the other by Safwan ibn Umayyah.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: "It has reached us that the verse of testing by which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) extended a truce to the disbelievers of Quraysh was because of the covenant that existed between the disbelievers of Quraysh and the Prophet (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) would return to the disbelievers of Quraysh what they had spent on their women who embraced Islam and emigrated, and their husbands were disbelievers under the covenant between the Prophet (ﷺ) and them. Had they been an enemy with no period of truce or agreement between them and the Prophet (ﷺ), he would not have returned anything of what they had spent. Allah ruled for the believers over the disbelievers of the truce in this manner." Allah said: ﴿O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, test them...﴾ until ﴿Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾. So the believers divorced, when this verse was revealed, every disbelieving woman who was under a man among them. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, divorced his wife, the daughter of Abu Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah from the Banu Makhzum, and Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan married her; and the daughter of Jarwal from Khuza'ah, whom Abu Jahm ibn Hudhayfah al-'Adawi married. Allah made this a ruling by which He judged between the believers and the polytheists during that period.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: al-Zuhri said: When this verse was revealed, "O you who have believed, when believing women come to you..." until His words "and do not hold on to marriage bonds with disbelieving women," among those whom 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, divorced was his wife, the close relative of Abu Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah, and after him Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan married her, while they were both still polytheists in Mecca. And Umm Kulthum, the daughter of Jarwal al-Khuza'iyyah, the mother of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, was married by Abu Jahm ibn Hudhayfah ibn Ghanim, a man of his people, while they were both still polytheists. And Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn 'Amr al-Taymi had Arwa bint Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib as his wife, and Islam separated them when the Qur'an forbade holding on to disbelieving women's bonds. Talhah had emigrated while she was in Mecca on the religion of her people. Then after Talhah, she was married in Islam by Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As ibn Umayyah ibn 'Abd Shams. Among the disbelieving women who fled to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), from those with whom he had no covenant, he detained her and gave her in marriage to a man among the Muslims: Umaymah bint Bishr al-Ansariyyah. Then one of the women of Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd from Aws Allah, who had been married to Thabit ibn al-Dahdaha, fled from him while he was then a disbeliever to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave her in marriage to Sahl ibn Hunayf of Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, and she bore 'Abd Allah ibn Sahl.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, regarding Allah's words: ﴿And do not hold on to marriage bonds with disbelieving women﴾, he said: al-Zuhri said: 'Umar divorced two wives he had in Mecca.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And do not hold on to marriage bonds with disbelieving women﴾: he said: The companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) were commanded to divorce their disbelieving wives in Mecca, who remained with the disbelievers.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And do not hold on to marriage bonds with disbelieving women﴾: the polytheist Arab women who refuse Islam; he was commanded to let them go free.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And do not hold on to marriage bonds with disbelieving women﴾: if the woman disbelieves, do not keep her; release her. Separation occurred between her and her husband when she disbelieved.

The reciters differed regarding the reading of His words: ﴿And do not hold on to﴾. The majority of reciters of the Hijaz, Madinah, Kufa and Syria read ﴿wa-la tumsikū﴾ with a light sīn. Abu 'Amr read ﴿wa-la tumassikū﴾ with a doubled sīn, and it is mentioned that this is the reading of al-Hasan, and whoever read it with the light form took as evidence the words ﴿wa-imsākun bi-ma'rūf﴾.

The correct view on this is that both are well-known readings and established dialects, reported from the Arabs: amsaktu bihi and maskatu, and tamassaktu bihi.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And ask for what you have spent, and let them ask for what they have spent﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the husbands of those wives who joined the polytheists to Mecca from the abode of Islam, from the disbelieving Quraysh: Ask, O believers whose wives have gone and joined the polytheists, for what you spent on your wives who joined them, of the bridal payment, from those who married them among them. And let the polytheists among those whose wives joined you as believers ask you, when their wives married among you, for what they spent on them of the bridal payment.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: The believers acknowledged the judgement of Allah and paid what they were commanded to pay of the polytheists' expenses which they had spent on their women, but the polytheists refused to acknowledge the judgement of Allah concerning what was imposed on them of paying the Muslims' expenses.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding Allah's words: ﴿And ask for what you have spent, and let them ask for what they have spent﴾: he said: Whatever of the wives of the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) went to the disbelievers, the disbelievers should give their bridal payments and keep them; and whatever of the wives of the disbelievers went to the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), it is similar, in the treaty that existed between Muhammad (ﷺ) and Quraysh.

* *

As for His words: ﴿That is the judgement of Allah; He judges between you﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: This is the ruling I have issued among you, O believers, concerning asking the polytheists for what you spent on your wives who joined them, and their command to ask you likewise concerning their wives who joined you: the judgement of Allah between you, so do not transgress it, for it is the truth which nothing else is heard in place of. The believers among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), it is related, submitted to the command and judgement of Allah, while the polytheists refused it and demanded fulfilment of the conditions they had stipulated between them in that treaty. The reports and accounts from the historians and others have come with this.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr informed us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: As for the believers, they acknowledged the judgement of Allah; as for the polytheists, they refused to acknowledge it. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And if any of your wives escape to the disbelievers...﴾ the verse.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, who said: Allah said: ﴿That is the judgement of Allah; He judges between you﴾. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) withheld the women and returned the men, and asked from the women's bridal payments of those who had been withheld, that the one whom Allah commanded him to ask should be asked, and that they should return to them the like of what they return to them if they did so. Had it not been for this judgement that Allah ruled, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would have returned the women as he returned the men. And had it not been for the truce and covenant that existed between him and Quraysh on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, he would have withheld the women and not returned any bridal payment to them; and so he would do with Muslim women who came to him before the covenant. As for His words: ﴿And Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾, He, may His praise be exalted, says: Allah is possessed of knowledge of what sets right His creation and other matters, and Wise in His management of them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 60, verse 11:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if any of your wives go over to the disbelievers, and you then have a retaliation [victory], give to those whose wives have gone the like of what they had spent. And fear Allah, in whom you are believers.﴾ (60:11)

He, may His praise be exalted, says to the believers among the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: ﴿And if any of your wives go over﴾ O believers, ﴿to the disbelievers﴾ and join them.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the disbelievers referred to in His saying ﴿to the disbelievers﴾: who are they? Some of them said: they are the disbelievers with whom there was no covenant between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They said: the meaning of the speech is: "And if any of your wives go over to those disbelievers with whom you have no covenant."

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿And if any of your wives go over to the disbelievers﴾: those with whom there is no covenant between you and them.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And if any of your wives go over to the disbelievers﴾, when they flee from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ to disbelievers with whom there is no covenant between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Mujahid: ﴿And if any of your wives go over to the disbelievers﴾, he said: there was no covenant between them.

Others said: rather, they are the disbelievers of Quraysh who were people of a truce (hudnah), and that is the saying of al-Zuhri.

* Yunus related to me that, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Yunus informed me, from him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾

The reciters differed in reading it. The majority of the reciters of the cities read ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾ with an alif, on the pattern of fa'altum (fā'altum), meaning: you obtained a 'uqba (a turn of gain) from them. Humayd al-A'raj, as is reported from him, read ﴿fa-'aqqabtum﴾ on the pattern of fa'altum with a doubled qaf, and the two are, in their differing wording, like His saying: ﴿And do not turn your cheek away from people﴾ (wa la tusa'ir khaddaka), and tusa'ir, with their meanings being close.

Abu Ja'far said: the more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who reads ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾ with an alif, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Then give to those whose wives have gone the like of what they had spent﴾

He says: give to those whose wives have gone from among you to the disbelievers the like of what they spent on them as dower (sadaq).

The people of interpretation differed regarding the wealth from which they were commanded to give to the one whose wife went to the polytheists. Some said: they were commanded to give them the dower of those who joined them from the wives of the polytheists.

Mention of those who said that:

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Yunus informed me, from al-Zuhri, he said: The believers acknowledged the judgment of Allah and paid what they had been commanded of the expenditures of the polytheists which they had spent on their wives; and the polytheists refused to acknowledge the judgment of Allah regarding what was obligatory upon them of paying the expenditures of the Muslims. So Allah said to the believers: ﴿And if any of your wives go over to the disbelievers, and you then have a retaliation, give to those whose wives have gone the like of what they had spent. And fear Allah, in whom you are believers.﴾ So if, after this verse, a woman from the wives of the believers went over to the polytheists, the believers would return to her husband the expenditure he had spent on her from the 'aqab that was in their hands, which they had been commanded to return to the polytheists from their expenditures that they had spent on their wives who believed and emigrated; then they would return to the polytheists the surplus, if any remained for them. And 'aqab: what was in the hands of the believers of the dower of the wives of the disbelievers when they believed and emigrated.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, he said: Allah sent down ﴿And if any of your wives go over to the disbelievers, and you then have a retaliation, give to those whose wives have gone the like of what they had spent﴾, so Allah commanded the believers to return the dower when a woman of the Muslims went over, and whose husband (had a claim): the Muslims would return to him his wife's dower from the dower that was in their hands, of what they had been commanded to return to the polytheists.

Others said: rather, they were commanded to give him from the booty (ghanimah) or the spoils (fay').

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And if any of your wives go over to the disbelievers, and you then have a retaliation, give to those whose wives have gone the like of what they had spent. And fear Allah, in whom you are believers.﴾ He means: if a woman of a man among the emigrants joined the disbelievers, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that he be given from the booty the like of what he had spent.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, that they had been commanded to return to them from the booty. And Mujahid used to read: ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾.

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾ means: you obtained booty from Quraysh or others; ﴿then give to those whose wives have gone the like of what they had spent﴾: their dowers as compensation.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Mujahid: ﴿And if any of your wives go over to the disbelievers﴾, he said: from those with whom there is no covenant between them and you; if a woman went to the polytheists, her husband is given the mahr of her equivalent; ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾: then you obtained booty; ﴿fa-atu alladhina dhahabat azwajuhum mithla ma anfaqu wa-ttaqu Allah﴾, he said: the mahr of her equivalent is given to her husband.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿And if any of your wives go over to the disbelievers, and you then have a retaliation, give to those whose wives have gone the like of what they had spent. And fear Allah﴾: they, when they fled from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ to the disbelievers with whom there was no covenant between them and the Prophet of Allah, then the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ obtained booty; he gave her husband what he had paid to her from the entire booty, then they divided their booty.

* Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to me, he said: al-Qasim related to us, he said: I heard al-Kisa'i report from Za'idah, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq that he read it ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾ and explained it as "then you took booty."

* Ahmad related to us, he said: al-Qasim related to us, he said: Hushaym related to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, concerning His saying ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾: he said: you took booty.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: We asked al-Zuhri about this verse and Allah's saying in it: ﴿And if any of your wives go over to the disbelievers﴾ ... the verse. He said: He says: if one of you has a wife who goes over to the disbelievers, and no wife comes to you whom you may take in exchange for what they take from you, then compensate him from fay' if you obtain it.

Others said regarding this:

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿And if any of your wives go over to the disbelievers, and you then have a retaliation﴾: a woman from the people of Islam went out to the polytheists, and no one else went out with her. Then a woman from the polytheists came, and the people said: "This is your 'uqbah (exchange) that has come to you." So Allah said: ﴿And if any of your wives go over to the disbelievers, and you then have a retaliation﴾: you retain what came to you from them on account of what you have with them. ﴿Then give to those whose wives have gone the like of what they had spent﴾. Then Allah informed them that there is no blame upon them if they do what they did, to marry them once their wombs have been cleared. He said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ then called the one whose wife had gone to the disbelievers and said to this woman who had come from the polytheists: "Is this the husband of the one who went? I will marry him to you?" She said: "O Messenger of Allah, God excused this man's wife for fleeing from him; no, by Allah, I have no need of him." Then he called al-Bukhturi, a large man, and said: "This one?" She said: "Yes," and she was of those who came from Mecca.

The most correct of these sayings, in terms of truth, is to say: Allah, mighty and majestic, commanded in this verse the believers to give to the one whose wife fled from the believers to the people of disbelief, if they had a 'uqba over the people of disbelief, either by booty they obtain from them, or by the joining of some of their women to them, the like of what they had spent upon the one who fled from them to them. He did not specify that giving of that from one kind of wealth rather than another; so they must give them that from all the wealth we have mentioned.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And fear Allah, in whom you are believers﴾

He says: and fear Allah, in whom you, O believers, are believers (i.e., those who affirm Him), so fear Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 60, verse 12:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse, nor kill their children, nor bring a slander they have invented between their hands and their feet, nor disobey you in what is right, then accept their pledge and ask Allah for forgiveness for them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (12).

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you﴾ [believing in Allah] ﴿pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse, nor kill their children, nor bring a slander they have invented between their hands and their feet﴾. He says: nor bring a lie they fabricate about a newborn found between their hands and their feet. The meaning of the speech is: nor attribute to their husbands children who are not theirs.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿nor bring a slander they have invented between their hands and their feet﴾, he says: nor attribute to their husbands children other than their own.

* * *

And His words: ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾

He says: nor disobey you, O Muhammad, in what is right from the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which you enjoin upon them. It is mentioned that this "what is right" in which they were stipulated not to disobey the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is wailing (al-niyaha).

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali related to us, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiya told us, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾, he says: that they not wail (la yunhan).

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak told us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, regarding ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾, he said: the wailing.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, from Mansur, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, the like of it.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir told us, from Mansur, from Salim, the like of it.

* Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Muharibi related to us, he said: Musa ibn Umayr told us, from Abu Salih, regarding His words: ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾, he said: in wailing.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾, he said: the wailing.

* He said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Zayd ibn Aslam, ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾, he said: they shall not scratch a face, nor tear a collar, nor call out "woe," nor recite poetry.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The testing of the women was that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), saying: Say to them: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pledges allegiance to you that you will not associate anything with Allah. Hind bint Utba ibn Rabi'a, who had split open the belly of Hamza (may Allah have mercy on him), was among the women disguised, and she said: If I speak, he will recognize me, and if he recognizes me, he will kill me. She had only disguised herself out of fear of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So the women with Hind fell silent and refused to speak. Hind, while disguised, said: How can he accept from women something he did not accept from men? So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at her and said to Umar: Say to them: ﴿nor steal﴾. Hind said: By Allah, I take from Abu Sufyan some small things [[In Ibn Kathir (6: 207): hinah, in the singular, meaning a small thing; its plural is hinat and hinawat]], and I do not know whether they are lawful for me or not. Abu Sufyan said: Whatever you have taken of what has passed, or what remains, it is lawful for you. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed and recognized her, and called her, and she came. She took his hand and sought refuge with him. He said: You are Hind. She said: Allah has pardoned what has passed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned away from her, and he said: ﴿nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾. She said: O Messenger of Allah, does a free woman commit fornication? He said: No, by Allah, a free woman does not commit fornication. He said: ﴿nor kill their children﴾. Hind said: You killed them at Badr, so you and they know best. He said: ﴿nor bring a slander they have invented between their hands and their feet, nor disobey you in what is right﴾. He said: He forbade them to wail. The women of the Jahiliyya used to tear their garments, scratch their faces, cut their hair, and call out for destruction and woe.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you﴾ until ﴿then accept their pledge﴾: it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) took from them that day the pledge not to wail, and not to speak with men except a man of them who is a mahram. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said: O Prophet of Allah, we have guests, and we are absent from our women. He said: The Messenger of Allah said: "Those are not what I meant."

* Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾, he said: it is wailing; they were taken to pledge that they would not wail, nor be alone in speech with men except with a mahram. He said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said: We are absent and we have guests. He said: "Those are not what I meant."

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Sulayman told us, he said: Abu Hilal informed us, he said: Qatada told us, regarding His words: ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾, he said: she should not speak with a man.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Ayyash related to me, from Sulayman ibn Sulayman, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "Umayma bint Ruqayqa came to the Prophet (ﷺ) pledging allegiance to him for Islam. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to her: I pledge to you that you will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse, nor kill your child, nor bring a slander you invent between your hands and your feet, nor wail, nor display yourself as the women of the first Jahiliyya did."

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Umayma bint Ruqayqa, who said: "Women came to the Prophet (ﷺ) to pledge allegiance to him. He said: In what you are able and capable of. We said: Allah and His Messenger are more merciful to us than we are to ourselves."

* Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam related to us, he said: My father and Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth related to us, from al-Layth, he said: Khalid ibn Yazid related to us, from Ibn Abi Hilal, from Ibn al-Munkadir, that Umayma informed him that she entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with women, and they said: O Messenger of Allah, extend your hand that we may shake it. He said: "I do not shake hands with women, but I will take your pledge." He took our pledge until he reached ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾, and he said: "In what you are able and capable of." We said: Allah is more merciful to us than we are to ourselves.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Harun told us, from Amr, from Asim, from Ibn Sirin, from Umm Atiyya al-Ansariyya, who said: "Among what was stipulated upon us as right when he took our pledge was that we should not wail. A woman from the family of so-and-so said: The family of so-and-so made me happy (by mourning with me), so let me repay them. She went and made them happy, then came and pledged. He said: None of them fulfilled it except her and Umm Sulaym daughter of Milhan, the mother of Anas ibn Malik."

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Abu Nu'aym told us, he said: Amr ibn Furukh al-Qattat told us, he said: Musab ibn Nuh al-Ansari told us, he said: "I met an old woman of ours who was among those who pledged to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). She said: I came to him to pledge, and he took from us what he took, including: and do not wail. An old woman said: O Prophet of Allah, people had helped me in misfortunes that befell me, and now they have suffered a misfortune, so I want to help them. He said: Go and repay them. Then she came and pledged to him." He said: That is the right thing mentioned by Allah: ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' told us, from Yazid, mawla of al-Sahba', from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salama, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), regarding His words: ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾, she said: the wailing.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Yunus told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Umayma bint Ruqayqa al-Taymiyya, who said: "I pledged to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) among women of the Muslims. We said to him: We have come to you, O Messenger of Allah, to pledge to you that we will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse, nor kill our children, nor bring a slander we invent between our hands and our feet, nor disobey you in what is right. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'In what you are able and capable of.' We said: Allah and His Messenger are more merciful to us than we are to ourselves. We said: Pledge to us, O Messenger of Allah. He said: 'Go, for I have pledged to you. My word to a hundred women is like my word to one woman.' And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not shake hands with any of us."

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Yunus ibn Bukayr told us, from Isa ibn Abd Allah al-Tamimi, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Umayma bint Ruqayqa, maternal aunt of Fatima, daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "I heard her say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pledged us and took from us that we not associate anything with Allah," and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq.

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Umayma bint Ruqayqa, who said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) among women we were pledging. She said: The Prophet (ﷺ) took from us what is in the Qur'an: ﴿that they will not associate anything with Allah﴾... the verse. Then he said: 'In what you are able and capable of.' We said: O Messenger of Allah, will you not shake our hands? He said: 'I do not shake hands with women. My word to one woman is only like my word to a hundred women.'"

* Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi related to us, he said: Amr ibn Abi Salama told us, from Zuhayr, from Musa ibn Uqba, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Umayma bint Ruqayqa, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), similar to it.

* It was related to me, from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd told us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾: "what is right" is what was stipulated upon them in the pledge, that they follow his command.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding the words of Allah: ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is His prophet and the chosen one of His creation; then He did not make lawful for him any command except with a condition, which He did not say: nor disobey you, and leave it, until He said: in what is right. How then should anyone be obeyed in other than what is right, when Allah has stipulated this for His Prophet? He said: "What is right" is every right thing he commands them in all matters, and it is fitting for them not to disobey.

* Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz related to us, Ishaq ibn Idris told us, Ishaq ibn Uthman ibn Ya'qub told us, he said: Isma'il ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Atiyya related to me, from his grandmother Umm Atiyya, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Medina, he gathered the Ansari women in a house, then sent Umar ibn al-Khattab to us. He stood at the door and greeted us, and we returned his greeting, and he said: I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah to you. We said: Welcome to the Messenger of Allah and the messenger of the Messenger of Allah. He said: Will you pledge that you will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse? We said: Yes. He extended his hand from outside the door or house, and we extended our hands from inside the house, and he said: O Allah, bear witness. She said: We were commanded on the two festivals to bring out the menstruating women and the young unmarried women, and we were not obliged to attend Friday prayer, and we were forbidden to follow funeral processions. Isma'il said: I asked my grandmother about the words of Allah: ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾, and she said: wailing.

* Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi related to me, he said: Amr ibn Abi Salama told us, from Zuhayr, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾, he said: a man should not be alone with a woman.

* * *

And His words: ﴿then accept their pledge﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: When believing women come to you pledging on these conditions, then accept their pledge. ﴿And ask Allah for forgiveness for them﴾ means: ask Allah to pardon their sins and cover them for them by His forgiveness of them. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ means: indeed Allah is One who veils the sins of whoever repents to Him from his sins, so that He does not punish him for them after his repentance from them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 60, verse 13:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿O you who have believed, do not make allies of a people with whom Allah has become angry; they have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves (13)﴾

He, may He be remembered, says to the believers among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿O you who have believed, do not make allies of a people with whom Allah has become angry﴾, [meaning] of the Jews, ﴿they have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves﴾.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿they have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: these people with whom Allah has become angry, from among the Jews, have despaired of Allah's reward in the Hereafter, and of being raised up, just as the living disbelievers have despaired of their dead who are in the graves of returning to them.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not make allies of a people with whom Allah has become angry﴾ ... the verse, meaning: whoever of those who disbelieved has died, the living have despaired of them returning to them, or of Allah raising them.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur ibn Zadhan, from al-Hasan, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿they have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves﴾, he said: the living disbelievers have despaired of the dead.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿they have despaired of the Hereafter﴾, he says: they have despaired of being raised, just as the disbelievers have despaired of the people in the graves, who died, returning to them.

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not make allies of a people with whom Allah has become angry, they have despaired of the Hereafter﴾ ... the verse: the disbeliever does not hope to meet his dead nor his reward.

I was told by al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying: ﴿they have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves﴾: whoever of those who disbelieved has died, the living have despaired of them returning to them, or of Allah raising them.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: they have despaired of the Hereafter, that Allah would show them mercy therein and forgive them, just as the disbelievers who are the people of graves, who have died and gone to the graves, have despaired of Allah's mercy and His pardon toward them in the Hereafter, because they have become certain of Allah's punishment for them.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, concerning this verse: ﴿they have despaired of the Hereafter﴾ ... the verse, he said: the people of the graves, who are in the graves, have despaired of the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to me; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿they have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves﴾, he said: from the reward of the Hereafter, when their deeds became clear to them and they witnessed the Fire.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah that he said concerning this verse: ﴿they have despaired of the Hereafter﴾ ... the verse, he said: the people of the graves have despaired of the Hereafter.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, he said: al-Kalbi said: ﴿they have despaired of the Hereafter﴾, meaning the Jews and the Christians, he says: they have despaired of the reward of the Hereafter and its honour, just as the disbelievers who have died and are in the graves have despaired of Paradise when they saw their place in the Fire.

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning Allah's saying: ﴿do not make allies of a people﴾ ... the verse: these disbelievers have despaired of there being a Hereafter for them, just as the disbelievers who died, who are in the graves, have despaired of there being a Hereafter for them, because of what they witnessed of the matter of the Hereafter. So just as those disbelievers despaired, so too have these disbelievers despaired. He said: and the people with whom Allah has become angry are their Jews, who have despaired of there being a Hereafter for them, just as the disbelievers before them among the people of the graves did, because they had known the Book of Allah, and persisted in disbelief in it, and in what they did while they knew.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, concerning His saying: ﴿they have despaired of the Hereafter﴾ ... the verse, he said: they have despaired of there being for them the reward of the Hereafter, just as those in the graves among the disbelievers have despaired of good, when they witnessed the punishment and humiliation.

The most correct of the two views in my opinion is the view of the one who said: these people with whom Allah has become angry, from among the Jews, have despaired of Allah's reward for them in the Hereafter and His honour, because of their disbelief and their denial of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), while knowing that he is a Prophet of Allah, just as the disbelievers among them who passed away before them and perished, and became the people of the graves, have despaired of Allah's reward and honour for them, while they were upon the like of what these are upon of denying Jesus, peace be upon him, and the other Messengers.

We only said that this is the more correct of the two views regarding the interpretation of the verse, because the dead have despaired of returning to the world, or of being raised before the Establishment of the Hour, the believers and the disbelievers alike; so there is no reason to restrict this report to the disbelievers, when the believers share with them in despair of that.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Mumtahanah.
